body:
Most delivery problems come from two causes: a small mistake in the address, or no one being available to sign. Both are easy to avoid if you know what to check, and avoiding them can save you weeks of delay and the cost of a returned parcel. This guide explains how to enter your address exactly, how to choose a place where an adult will be, how to handle apartments, gated communities and workplaces, why P.O. boxes do not work, how the name on the package matters, what to do if you will be away and how to fix a mistake. It follows our published [shipping policy](/shipping/) and is written for adults aged 21 and over.

## Use the exact address
Enter your address as it appears on your mail. Include the apartment, suite or unit number in the second address line, the full five-digit ZIP code and the correct city and state. Mismatches cause delays and returns. If the street name has a direction, such as North or SW, include it. If your address has changed recently, use the new one and check that the carrier will recognize it. Copy it from a recent bill or a mail label if you are unsure.

### Common address mistakes
- **Missing apartment or unit number,** which leaves the carrier unable to find the right door.
- **Wrong ZIP code,** which can send the parcel to the wrong facility.
- **Abbreviations that the carrier cannot read,** such as an unusual street suffix.
- **A different name on the mailbox,** so the carrier cannot match the recipient.
- **An old address,** especially after a move.

## Choose a place where an adult will be
Every package needs an adult aged 21 or older to sign with photo ID. A home address where someone is present during the day, or a workplace that allows personal deliveries, usually works best. If you are rarely home during the day, consider whether a trusted adult, a neighbor you know well or your workplace can receive it. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) for how the signing works.

## Gated communities and apartment buildings
Add gate codes, buzzer numbers and building notes in the order notes. Tell your building staff or neighbors to expect a delivery that needs a signature, because the carrier cannot leave the parcel at the door. If a front desk accepts packages, ask whether staff can sign for an adult-signature parcel, since many cannot. If they cannot, the carrier will need to reach you, so keep your phone number accurate and your phone on.

## Avoid P.O. boxes
Carriers cannot obtain a signature at a P.O. box. Use a street address instead. For the same reason, parcel lockers and some mailbox stores may not work for adult-signature deliveries. If you are unsure whether an address will work, ask us before you order.

## Name on the package
Use the name on your ID. Some carriers require the recipient's name to match the ID when they check it, and a mismatch can lead to a refused delivery. If another adult will receive the parcel, tell us in the order notes and check with the carrier. Use the same name on the order and on the doorbell or mailbox where you can, so the carrier is not confused.

## Phone number and email
Your phone number lets the carrier reach you if the address needs clarifying or a delivery needs rescheduling. Enter it with the area code, and keep it on during the delivery window. Your email receives our confirmations, tracking and your private link, so check it carefully. See [why we need your email and phone](/blog/why-we-need-your-email-and-phone/).

## Where we do not ship
Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands and military addresses are excluded from free shipping, and we do not ship internationally. Some states and cities restrict certain products, and we cannot ship where the law does not allow it. See [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

## If you will be away
If you will be away when the parcel is likely to arrive, tell us right away through the [contact page](/contact/), and consider delaying payment so the order does not process until you are back, or arranging for a trusted adult to receive it. A parcel that cannot be signed for is returned, and the refund is minus the 15% restocking fee and the shipping cost. Planning avoids that loss. See [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/).

## After you order
Watch for the tracking email, and open the carrier's tracking page when it arrives. Many carriers let you set up delivery alerts or choose a delivery window. Keep your ID ready, and make sure someone is available. If you see a delivery notice, follow the instructions at once. See [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/) and [what to do if your package is delayed](/blog/what-to-do-if-your-package-is-delayed/).

## A pre-order checklist
1. Is the street address complete and spelled correctly?
2. Is the apartment or unit number in the second line?
3. Is the ZIP code correct?
4. Is the name the same as on my ID?
5. Will an adult aged 21 or older be there to sign?
6. Is my phone number correct, and will my phone be on?
7. Have I added gate codes or building notes?
8. Is my email correct?

## Fixing a mistake
If you notice a mistake after you order, contact us immediately with your order ID and the corrected address, and wait for our written confirmation. Before the parcel is handed to the carrier, we can usually correct it. After that, we cannot change the address, and the carrier may return the parcel. See [how to change or cancel an order](/blog/how-to-change-or-cancel-an-order/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I use a work address?
Often yes, if your employer allows personal deliveries and an adult will be available to sign. Check your workplace rules first.

### What if my building has a package room?
A package room cannot take adult-signature parcels unless a staff member can sign. Ask your building staff, and give the carrier a way to reach you.

### What if I live in a rural area?
Delivery to rural addresses can take longer, and some carriers have limited coverage. Contact us with your address if you are unsure, and we will tell you what customers there typically see.

### What if my name is long or has special characters?
Enter it as it appears on your ID, and use plain letters where the form requires. If a carrier cannot read it, it may cause delays.

Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A worked example: a missed signature
A customer in an apartment building orders a parcel and enters the street address but forgets the unit number. The carrier arrives, cannot find the right door and cannot reach the customer, because the phone number has a typo. After two attempts the parcel is returned. The customer receives a refund minus the 15% restocking fee and the shipping cost, and has to order again and wait another two weeks. Two small errors, a missing unit number and a mistyped phone number, caused the whole delay. A thirty-second check before submitting would have prevented it.

## Habits that prevent most problems
Read the address back before you submit, preferably aloud. Compare it with a recent piece of mail. Check the phone number digit by digit. Tell anyone who lives with you or works nearby to expect a delivery that needs a signature. And save the tracking email so you can follow the parcel. These habits take a minute, and they make the difference between a smooth delivery and a returned one.

## Frequently asked questions about delivery windows
### Can I choose a delivery time?
That depends on the carrier. Some carriers let you pick a window or request a redelivery through their tracking page. Adult-signature parcels sometimes have fewer options, so check the carrier's page as soon as your tracking email arrives.

### Can I pick up the parcel from the carrier?
Some carriers hold a parcel at a facility after a missed delivery, and you can collect it with your ID. Follow the instructions on the delivery notice, and do it quickly, because holds are limited in time.

### What if I have a dog or a locked gate?
Make sure the carrier can reach the door, and add instructions in the order notes. A dog that prevents access can lead to a failed delivery attempt. Secure pets before the likely delivery window.

### Should I tell my neighbors?
If you share a building or a street with people who might sign, let them know a delivery is coming, and remind them that a parcel needing an adult signature should be handed to you, not left. Better still, be there yourself.

## Special cases
**Dormitories and shared houses.** Use the full building and room details, and make sure a resident aged 21 or older will sign. Some campuses restrict deliveries of age-restricted products, so check the rules first.

**Businesses with reception desks.** Ask whether the front desk may sign for an adult-signature parcel. If not, arrange for you or a colleague to receive it in person.

**Recently built addresses.** If your street is new, check that the carrier recognizes it, and add a note with the nearest cross street if needed.

faq.q: Where do I put the apartment number?
faq.a: In the second address line, together with the full ZIP code, so the carrier can find the exact door.

faq.q: Why can't I ship to a P.O. box?
faq.a: Adult signature is required, and a carrier cannot obtain a signature at a P.O. box.

faq.q: Whose name should be on the package?
faq.a: The name on the ID of the adult who will sign. Some carriers require the names to match.

faq.q: What if I live in an apartment building?
faq.a: Add gate codes, buzzer numbers and building notes in the order notes, and ask whether staff can sign for adult-signature parcels.

faq.q: What if I will be away?
faq.a: Tell us right away, consider delaying payment or arrange for a trusted adult to receive it. A parcel nobody signs for is returned.

faq.q: What if I made a mistake in the address?
faq.a: Contact us immediately with your order ID and the corrected address. We can usually fix it before the parcel is handed to the carrier.
